hero.lead: Houston to Miami is about two and a half hours nonstop from Bush Intercontinental or Hobby. One Monday-to-Thursday week, 20 porcelain veneers made in our own lab, and a 5-year warranty in writing for the flight home.
hero.alt: Miami seen from an airplane window on approach to Miami International Airport
hero.caption: IAH or HOU → MIA · about 2 h 30 min nonstop · 15 minutes from the airport to the clinic

intro: Houston has two airports with nonstop flights to Miami: Bush Intercontinental (IAH) with the most departures, and Hobby (HOU), closer to downtown and the Medical Center. Either way the flight is about two and a half hours, and you land 15 minutes from the clinic. The whole week runs in Spanish or English.

Many Houston patients arrive with a quote in hand, often for crowns, and want a second opinion on the material and how much tooth is removed. Our answer goes in writing before you book: [porcelain veneers](/porcelain-veneers-miami) at about 0.3 mm of preparation, made in the [lab in our building](/custom-lab), or the 20-veneer [Smile Design](/smile-design-miami) at {price}. Hotels, airport and what to pack are on the [out-of-state patients page](/out-of-state-patients).

gettingHere.title: Getting from Houston to the clinic
gettingHere.aside: General guidance from the clinic. Check times and carriers with the airline when you book; we do not sell flights.

items.d: About 2 hours 30 to 2 hours 45 minutes nonstop. There is a one-hour time change: Miami is on Eastern time, an hour ahead of Houston, so a 7 am departure lands around 11:30 am local.

United and American fly IAH–MIA nonstop through the day. Southwest flies Hobby (HOU) to MIA. Fort Lauderdale (FLL) is an alternative with more low-cost carriers, about 45 minutes to an hour from the clinic.

MIA is 15 minutes away by car. Uber and Lyft pick up at arrivals; we text you the spot and the clinic address before you land. The partner hotels are within 10 minutes of the clinic, so no rental car is needed.
Houston to Miami is about 1,200 miles along I-10 and I-75, close to nineteen hours of driving. It is not a realistic option for a four-day week; fly.

itinerary.title: A sample Monday-to-Thursday from Houston
itinerary.intro: Times are examples, in local time at each end, to show how the week fits with the one-hour time change. Any flight that lands by early afternoon Monday and leaves after 4 pm Thursday works.

days.d: Leave IAH around 7:00 am Monday, land MIA about 11:30 am Eastern, rideshare to the clinic for an early-afternoon Visit 1: exam, cleaning, X-rays, scans and the design preview. Or fly Sunday and come in rested.
days.time: Visit 1 about 1:00 pm to 3:00 pm Monday

days.d: About 0.3 mm of preparation and temporaries in the shape you approved. Soft lunch nearby, then the afternoon is free.

days.t: Free day while the lab finishes
days.d: Veneers milled, sintered and finished by hand upstairs. You tell us anything you would change about the temporaries before Thursday.

days.t: Delivery, then the evening flight home
days.d: Shade checked with the ceramist, veneers bonded, bite adjusted, warranty in writing. Lunch, rideshare to MIA.
days.time: Visit 3 about 9:00 am to 11:00 am. Fly MIA–IAH from about 4:00 pm Eastern, land Houston around 6:30 pm Central.

itinerary.note: With the time change, an early Monday flight still lands in time for an afternoon Visit 1. If you would rather not fly and sit in the chair on the same day, come Sunday; the Sunday hotel night is the only difference.

cost.body: Treatment is priced from the [published price list](/veneers-cost-miami) and confirmed in writing before you book. Travel is yours to book; we do not quote fares because they change daily.

items.q: Can I fly home to Houston the same day as delivery?
items.a: Yes. Thursday delivery takes about two hours in the morning and the bonding is final when you stand up. A flight after 4 pm Eastern gets you to IAH or Hobby by about 6:30 pm Central, with no rush at either end.

items.q: Does the time change affect the schedule?
items.a: Only on Monday. Miami is an hour ahead of Houston, so a 7 am flight lands at 11:30 am local and Visit 1 is early afternoon. We set the Monday appointment around your arrival time when you book.

items.q: I was quoted crowns for my whole smile in Houston. Is that the same thing?
items.a: No. A crown removes 60 to 70% of the tooth; a veneer removes about 0.3 mm from the front. Send us the quote with your photos and the plan you get back names, tooth by tooth, which need a veneer and whether any genuinely needs a crown.

items.q: Can the whole thing be done in Spanish?
items.a: Yes. The doctors, the coordinator and the lab work in Spanish and English, the estimate and the warranty come in either language, and this site is at /es for your family at home.

items.q: What if I need an adjustment once I am back in Houston?
items.a: There is a video check-in two weeks after delivery. Small adjustments are covered by the {warrantyYears}-year warranty at any dentist near you; anything larger, we bring you back.

items.q: Is it worth flying when there are clinics in Houston?
items.a: Only you can say, but compare the same five things in writing: material, number of teeth, veneer or crown per tooth, total, and warranty. Ours are on the price list. Then add two flights and three hotel nights and compare the totals, not the headline price.
